answer: Here is one mechanism that works: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because sparrow only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, island is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any orchard approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
